'''''Thymus capitellatus''''' is a species of flowering plant in the mint family [[Lamiaceae]], [[endemic]] to [[Portugal]].

==Description==
''Thymus capitellatus'' is a [[subshrub]] up to {{cvt|50|cm}} tall, erect. It has long, graceful stems, quadrangular in section, with very short hairs. Leaves are {{cvt|3.5|-|5.5|x|1|-|2|mm}}, with a [[tomentose]] underside and yellowish spheroidal glands; petiolated. Inflorescence is {{cvt|8|-|17|mm}}. Corolla up to {{cvt|8|mm}}, white or cream color. Purple stamens. n = 15.<ref name="iberica">{{cite web |title=''Thymus capitellatus'' |url=http://www.floraiberica.es/floraiberica/texto/pdfs/12_140_21_Thymus.pdf |publisher=[[Flora Iberica]] |access-date=31 March 2021|lang=es}}</ref>

==Distribution and habitat==
''Thymus capitellatus'' is native to southwest [[Portugal]] and is strongly present around the [[Tagus Estuary Natural Reserve|Tagus Estuary]] and [[Sado Estuary Natural Reserve|Sado Estuary]], inhabiting [[moorland]]s, xerophilic scrub ([[cistus]], [[heaths]]) and sometimes in pine, eucalyptus and acacia forests, colonizing sandy acid soils of a dune nature and above all paleodunes (stabilized dunes).<ref name="iucn status 12 November 2021" /><ref name="iberica" /><ref name="flora-on">{{cite web |title=''Thymus capitellatus'' Hoffmanns. & Link |url=https://flora-on.pt/#/1Thymus+capitellatus |publisher=[[Flora-On]] |access-date=31 March 2021 |lang=pt}}</ref>
